cases.name: Emily Pike
cases.about:
Emily was a member of the San Carlos Apache Tribe. After her death, Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs signed “Emily’s Law,” a bill that would establish an alert system for endangered people and tribal members under 65 who have vanished under suspicious circumstances in the state.

Emily’s aunt Carolyn Pike-Bender says she wants her niece, who loved pink, sparkly things, shopping, art and her cat, to be remembered as a happy teen with a big smile.

“She was just leaving the little girl stage, going into the preteen stage, but yet, not yet fully teenager-wise,” she says. “She was trying to find herself, but she was also trying to be a mother and a big sister to her younger siblings. She was getting in the age of liking boys.”
cases.narrative:
On 2/14/2025, her dismembered remains were discovered in two trash bags by Gila County sheriff’s deputies near Forest Road 355 on state land near the San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation in Arizona. Investigators were unable to find her arms and hands. An autopsy determined she died from "homicidal violence with blunt head trauma."

Emily was last seen walking near Mesa Dr and McKellips Rd in Mesa, AZ.
